question: Which of the following is a properly written SMART objective for a surgical ward?

options.A: Try harder to answer call bells quickly
options.B: Reduce post-operative wound infections by 15 percent within six months
options.C: Improve nursing care across the entire hospital soon
options.D: Make patients happier whenever they stay in the ward

explanation: This statement is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound with a clear deadline. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of these traits tells us that a material is hazardous waste?

options.A: Biodegradable
options.B: Odorless
options.C: Flammable
options.D: Transparent

explanation: That's right! Materials that are flammable, corrosive, toxic, or reactive are flagged as hazardous and heavily regulated. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h4)

question: Why do the veins in your limbs have one-way valves inside them?

options.A: To filter out dangerous toxins before blood enters the lungs
options.B: To store extra blood volume when a person is resting
options.C: To speed up blood flow as it leaves the left ventricle
options.D: To help push blood upward against gravity back toward the heart

explanation: Getting blood from your toes back up to your chest is a tough uphill battle against gravity! Vein valves act like little trapdoors that stop blood from sliding backward. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h8)

question: Why is keeping accurate family planning records so important for your clinic?

options.A: It allows nurses to diagnose complex reproductive tract infections
options.B: It determines the individual salary scale of clinic staff
options.C: It helps prevent stockouts by ensuring proper commodity forecasting
options.D: It replaces the need for physical client health folders

explanation: Spot on! When you track what is used, the district knows exactly when to send more supplies so you never run out of commodities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of sorting pregnant women into low-risk or high-risk groups at the clinic?

options.A: Eliminating the need for routine blood pressure checks
options.B: Determining the exact biological sex of the unborn child
options.C: Targeted management and appropriate referral when needed
options.D: Deciding the exact date the baby will be born

explanation: Exactly! Grouping mothers helps us give extra attention to those who need closer monitoring, and quickly refer complex cases to doctors when necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h2)

question: What is the most common type of fainting experienced by otherwise healthy people?

options.A: Vasovagal syncope
options.B: Orthostatic hypotension
options.C: Neurological syncope
options.D: Cardiac syncope

explanation: Vasovagal syncope is triggered by everyday events like pain, stress, or standing too long and affects most people who faint. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h2)

question: What is a major duty of the health orderly in the operating theatre?

options.A: Counting surgical needles before wound closure
options.B: Scrubbing in to assist the surgeon at the table
options.C: Administering intravenous fluids and medications
options.D: Transporting patients and heavy supplies safely

explanation: Health orderlies are essential for smooth operations—they handle patient transport, heavy lifting, waste disposal, and moving equipment. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h6)

question: Which nursing action helps prevent skin breakdown caused by oxygen mask straps?

options.A: Apply strong medical adhesive tape directly to the forehead
options.B: Remove the mask permanently and stop all oxygen therapy
options.C: Place protective padding under pressure points and check skin often
options.D: Pull the elastic straps tighter so the mask never shifts

explanation: Padding shares the load evenly across the skin, and checking frequently lets you spot irritation before it turns into a wound. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h7)

question: Which simple tool kit helps a nurse look clearly inside a patient's mouth?

options.A: A penlight and a tongue depressor
options.B: A flexible urinary catheter tube
options.C: A sterile lumbar puncture needle
options.D: A heavy metal reflex hammer

explanation: Keep it simple and practical! A penlight gives you light, and a tongue depressor helps you gently see every corner of the oral cavity. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h3)

question: A patient who struggles to walk is put in a room where a bedside table blocks the path to the toilet. What kind of risk is this blocked path?

options.A: Metabolic risk
options.B: Intrinsic risk
options.C: Extrinsic risk
options.D: Genetic risk

explanation: Extrinsic risks are environmental hazards outside the patient's body, like a blocked pathway in the room. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why is chronic kidney disease an important thing to note when taking a patient's blood history?

options.A: It triggers sudden and uncontrollable blood clotting
options.B: Damaged kidneys produce less erythropoietin, causing anaemia
options.C: It causes the liver to stop storing iron completely
options.D: Kidney failure immediately destroys all white blood cells

explanation: Healthy kidneys make erythropoietin, the hormone that tells the bone marrow to build red blood cells. When kidneys fail, that hormone drops, leading to anaemia. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h5)

question: A patient is brought in with no breathing and no pulse. What quick physical check confirms cardiac arrest?

options.A: Checking the skin color on the hands and feet
options.B: Measuring the blood pressure using an automated cuff
options.C: Testing the deep tendon reflexes in the knees
options.D: Auscultating the chest with a stethoscope for heart sounds

explanation: You got it! Listening directly to the chest with your stethoscope is a reliable way to check if heart sounds are completely gone. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h3)

question: What is the most crucial nursing action when caring for a patient having a severe endocrine emergency like a thyroid storm?

options.A: Closely monitoring vital signs and supporting stable organ function
options.B: Withholding prescribed medications until lab results return
options.C: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent swelling and weight gain
options.D: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to burn off excess energy

explanation: Endocrine emergencies cause wild, dangerous shifts in vitals and metabolism. Keeping a close eye on vital signs and giving steady supportive care is always your top priority. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T13#GNS222_U2_T13_h8)

question: Why must a triage nurse keep monitoring patients who are waiting in the emergency queue?

options.A: Doctors refuse to see patients without updated charts
options.B: Waiting patients often complain about the slow service
options.C: A stable patient's condition can suddenly get worse
options.D: Hospital policy requires a vital sign check every five minutes

explanation: Illness can change quickly! Someone who looks stable at first triage can crash suddenly and need immediate help. Keep a close eye on your patients. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h1)

question: Around how many weeks of pregnancy do morning sickness and nausea usually start?

options.A: 1 to 3 weeks
options.B: 16 to 18 weeks
options.C: 10 to 12 weeks
options.D: 4 to 6 weeks

explanation: You will often see this early in the first trimester around weeks 4 to 6, right when hormones start shooting up. Great job keeping this in mind for antenatal care! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h1)

question: Why is the living will movement considered a shift away from medical paternalism?

options.A: Because nurses take over the legal responsibilities of physicians
options.B: Because patients now direct their care instead of doctors making every choice
options.C: Because hospitals no longer require doctors to write treatment orders
options.D: Because family members now pay all medical bills directly

explanation: Traditional medical paternalism meant doctors decided everything. Living wills put the decision-making power back into the hands of the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of surgical asepsis compared to medical asepsis?

options.A: To replace the need for routine hand washing
options.B: To keep hospital room surfaces smelling fresh
options.C: To eliminate all microorganisms and spores completely
options.D: To reduce the number of visible dirt particles on skin

explanation: Surgical asepsis creates a sterile environment free of all life forms, including resistant bacterial spores, unlike medical asepsis which only reduces pathogen counts. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h5)

question: How does period prevalence differ from point prevalence?

options.A: It excludes patients who recovered before the study began
options.B: It only counts cases diagnosed by a doctor in a hospital
options.C: It includes cases present at any time during a set interval
options.D: It measures only brand-new infections over a lifetime

explanation: Period prevalence covers a span of time, capturing anyone who had the condition during that entire period. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h2)

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC)?

options.A: To investigate the legal cause of pregnancy termination
options.B: To treat complications from spontaneous or induced abortions
options.C: To perform mandatory psychological evaluations
options.D: To provide routine family planning counseling only

explanation: PAC is all about emergency medical support! It focuses on treating physical issues like heavy bleeding or infections so the patient can recover safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h1)

question: During which phase of the nursing process does the nurse actually perform interventions like wound care or medication administration?

options.A: Implementation
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Evaluation
options.D: Planning

explanation: Implementation is the action phase where the nurse carries out the planned care interventions. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why is the membrane inside the lungs where gas exchange happens so incredibly thin?

options.A: To allow the lungs to stretch easily during inhalation
options.B: To reduce the overall weight of the thoracic organs
options.C: To prevent white blood cells from entering the alveoli
options.D: To allow fast and efficient diffusion of gases

explanation: Spot on! A super thin wall means oxygen and carbon dioxide can zip back and forth between your lungs and blood instantly. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h3)

question: What does a fasting blood sugar test primarily measure?

options.A: Baseline blood glucose after food restriction
options.B: Maximum blood glucose right after a heavy meal
options.C: Average blood sugar over the last three months
options.D: Total amount of insulin stored in the pancreas

explanation: The test measures glucose levels when the body has not consumed calories for several hours, showing the true resting baseline. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h1)

question: What natural body process helps the uterus contract and shrink back down after delivery?

options.A: Oxytocin release stimulated by breastfeeding
options.B: Complete bed rest for the first week
options.C: Increased production of progesterone
options.D: Immediate resumption of heavy exercise

explanation: Amazing! When the baby suckles, the brain releases oxytocin. This hormone causes those strong, helpful uterine cramps that shrink the uterus and stop bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T021#GNS226_U3_T021_h2)

question: What happens during the progressive stage of shock?

options.A: Organs begin to regenerate damaged cells rapidly
options.B: Compensatory mechanisms fail and blood pressure drops
options.C: The body completely recovers its normal metabolic rate
options.D: Blood pressure rises above normal due to fluid retention

explanation: When compensation fails, blood pressure falls and perfusion to vital organs becomes dangerously low. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why do tablets or injections (systemic drugs) often struggle to treat eye problems effectively?

options.A: Blood vessels in the eye destroy active ingredients
options.B: Unique barriers like the cornea block them from getting inside
options.C: Systemic drugs cannot dissolve in body fluids
options.D: The liver breaks down all eye medications too quickly

explanation: Think of the eye as a well-guarded fort! Natural barriers like the cornea make it hard for drugs travelling through your bloodstream to get inside the eye in strong enough amounts. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h1)

question: How do common antipyretic drugs like paracetamol primarily lower a fever?

options.A: By blocking prostaglandin synthesis in the brain
options.B: By destroying bacteria in the bloodstream
options.C: By forcing the blood vessels in the skin to constrict
options.D: By directly cooling the skin through evaporation

explanation: Antipyretics stop the production of prostaglandins in the hypothalamus, which allows the body's internal thermostat to drop back down. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h4)

question: Your patient takes a traditional herbal remedy along with their prescribed blood pressure drugs. What should you do?

options.A: Explore the cultural significance of the remedy and check for potential drug interactions
options.B: Confiscate the herbal preparation during the home visit
options.C: Tell the patient immediately that traditional remedies are completely useless
options.D: Ignore the herbal remedy since it is not part of the hospital chart

explanation: Never dismiss cultural practices! Respect the patient while smartly checking to ensure the herbs won't clash with their prescribed medications. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h5)

question: Why is assessing the oral cavity a routine part of a general physical examination?

options.A: It is the only reliable way to measure a patient's exact daily caloric intake.
options.B: It allows the nurse to directly test the function of the respiratory lungs.
options.C: It gives quick clues about a patient's hydration, nutrition, and systemic health.
options.D: It confirms whether the patient has completely normal kidney filtration rates.

explanation: Oral tissues react quickly to changes in fluid balance, nutrition, and general disease, making the mouth a window into overall health. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h1)

question: A strict vegan diet without any supplements puts a patient at higher risk for which type of nutritional anaemia?

options.A: Inherited sickle cell anaemia
options.B: Vitamin B12 deficiency anaemia
options.C: Acute iron overload anaemia
options.D: Primary aplastic anaemia

explanation: Natural vitamin B12 is found mostly in animal products. Patients on a strict vegan diet need supplements or fortified foods to avoid getting B12 deficiency anaemia. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why must you shake a suspension bottle vigorously right before pouring a dose?

options.A: To cool down the liquid inside the glass container
options.B: To evenly redistribute settled solid drug particles
options.C: To check if the outer safety seal is broken
options.D: To create air bubbles that make the drug taste better

explanation: Shaking mixes the active medicine back into the liquid so the patient gets the right dose, not just flavored water! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h4)

question: How many total chromosomes are found in a normal human somatic cell?

options.A: 23 chromosomes
options.B: 46 chromosomes
options.C: 92 chromosomes
options.D: 48 chromosomes

explanation: Normal human body cells have 46 chromosomes organized into 23 pairs. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is giving plain water unnecessary for a fully breastfed infant living in a very hot climate?

options.A: Infants cannot swallow water safely during their first few months
options.B: Breast milk is made mostly of water and satisfies the infant's thirst
options.C: Hot weather stops the infant from feeling thirsty
options.D: Water causes immediate stomach pain in newborn babies

explanation: Breast milk contains about eighty-eight percent water, which is more than enough to keep a baby hydrated even in hot weather. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h1)

question: What is the primary site for nutrient absorption in the human body?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Small intestine
options.C: Esophagus
options.D: Large intestine

explanation: The small intestine has specialized structures that provide a massive surface area specifically designed for taking in digested nutrients. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why do nurses usually keep the head of the bed slightly elevated for a patient with high brain pressure?

options.A: To allow clearer visibility during frequent neurological checks
options.B: To help blood drain away from the head and lower pressure
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to swallow saliva safely
options.D: To prevent the lungs from collapsing during mechanical ventilation

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Elevating the head helps blood flow smoothly out of the brain, keeping intracranial pressure down. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which action is considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Keeping windows closed at night
options.B: Painting isolation walls white
options.C: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.D: Changing bed sheets twice a day

explanation: Handwashing with soap and water or using alcohol-based rub removes pathogens from hands before they spread to others. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which data collection method involves talking directly with trusted village leaders about local health issues?

options.A: Laboratory blood screenings
options.B: Key informant interviews
options.C: Direct environmental observation
options.D: Reviewing census registers

explanation: Key informants are knowledgeable community figures who provide deep insight into local health behaviors and needs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of these burns up the largest percentage of a typical person's daily calories?

options.A: Active voluntary movement
options.B: Basal Metabolic Rate
options.C: Formal athletic exercise
options.D: The thermic effect of food

explanation: Even if you sit still all day, your BMR uses up the vast majority of your daily calories just running your internal organs like your heart, brain, and lungs! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common sign of a vulnerable individual facing forced marriage?

options.A: Sudden and unexplained withdrawal from school or work
options.B: Eagerly volunteering to travel abroad alone for vacation
options.C: Showing intense fear when a family member speaks for them
options.D: Unexplained physical injuries or signs of ongoing abuse

explanation: Victims are often coerced or taken abroad against their will, rather than eagerly volunteering for independent vacations. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h4)

question: In inflammatory joint conditions, what is 'pannus'?

options.A: An abnormal tissue layer that destroys cartilage and bone
options.B: Fluid accumulation in the outer layer of the skin
options.C: Thickened scar tissue formed after a surgical incision
options.D: A hard calcium crystal deposit inside the joint space

explanation: Pannus is an extra layer of bad, granulation-like tissue that grows inside the joint and slowly eats away at the cartilage and bone. You'll often see this in conditions like rheumatoid arthritis! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h1)

question: How do daily routines and familiar activities help a patient with dementia during recovery?

options.A: They completely reverse brain cell death caused by Alzheimer's disease
options.B: They cure chronic sleep apnea permanently
options.C: They eliminate the need for any physical therapy exercises
options.D: They reduce confusion and help the patient feel secure enough to participate

explanation: Exactly right! Predictable routines calm anxiety and make confused patients feel safe enough to cooperate with care. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h5)

question: How is cancer grading different from cancer staging?

options.A: Grading counts white blood cells, while staging counts red blood cells
options.B: Grading is only used for benign tumors, while staging is for malignant ones
options.C: Grading looks at cellular appearance under a microscope, while staging looks at how far the cancer has spread
options.D: Grading measures organ failure, while staging measures treatment success

explanation: Think of it this way: Grading checks how 'wild' or abnormal the cells look under a microscope, while staging looks at the map of the body to see how far the cancer has traveled. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which structures are removed during a standard Type II FGM procedure?

options.A: The clitoris and the labia minora
options.B: The entire vulva and perineum
options.C: Only the pubic hair follicles
options.D: Only the vaginal mucous membrane

explanation: Type II goes a step further than Type I by removing both the clitoris and the labia minora (sometimes along with parts of the labia majora). [learn more](GNS312_U1_T3#GNS312_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is writing clear, real-time notes so important in emergency nursing?

options.A: It provides a clear legal record of all care provided
options.B: Doctors use the nurse's notes to diagnose diseases
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital insurance claim gets paid

explanation: Good documentation protects your patient's ongoing care and acts as legal proof in court of the great nursing care you delivered. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h7)

question: Which test is most commonly used to check hormone levels when doctors suspect an endocrine problem?

options.A: Serum blood tests
options.B: Lumbar punctures
options.C: Bone marrow biopsies
options.D: Sputum cultures

explanation: Correct! Drawing a sample of blood lets the lab measure the exact circulating amounts of specific hormones to see what's going on. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T15#GNS222_U2_T15_h2)

question: A woman with a history of Type III FGM comes in for labor. What should the nurse watch out for?

options.A: Total absence of uterine contractions throughout the first stage
options.B: Obstructed labor and severe scarring requiring careful evaluation
options.C: Spontaneous healing of the infibulated scar without intervention
options.D: Rapid and completely painless expulsion of the placenta

explanation: That thick scar tissue blocks the normal stretching of the birth canal, often causing obstructed labor that needs careful handling. Clinical nursing in action! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary diagnostic test used to record the electrical activity of the brain in seizure disorders?

options.A: Complete blood count (CBC)
options.B: Lumbar puncture (LP)
options.C: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.D: Electroencephalogram (EEG)

explanation: An EEG measures and records the brain's electrical wave patterns to help identify abnormal activity. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h5)

question: What is the main danger of atrial fibrillation?

options.A: The lungs fill with thick mucus
options.B: The heart stops all electrical activity forever
options.C: Blood can pool in the heart and form dangerous clots
options.D: Blood pressure rises past 200

explanation: In A-fib, the upper chambers of the heart just quiver instead of squeezing properly. When blood sits still like that, it forms clots that can travel to the brain. Scary stuff, but totally makes sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T14#GNS213_U1_T14_h3)

question: What should the nurse apply across the incision after removing sutures to provide extra support?

options.A: Sterile adhesive strips
options.B: Tight elastic bandages
options.C: Thick plaster of paris
options.D: Wet saline gauze pads

explanation: Adhesive closure strips help hold the skin edges together gently while the deeper layers continue gaining strength after suture removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why does the timing of certain reproductive health tests matter so much?

options.A: Infection rates are highest right after ovulation occurs
options.B: Hospitals only have laboratory reagents available on specific days of the month
options.C: Patients are too weak to undergo procedures during the first week of bleeding
options.D: Hormone levels and uterine lining thickness change during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Exactly! Hormones and tissue structures shift naturally all month long, so tests need to be timed right to get accurate results. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h1)

question: What fills the chest space when a patient has a hemothorax?

options.A: Air
options.B: Serous fluid
options.C: Blood
options.D: Pus

explanation: Easy and clear! 'Hemo' means blood, and 'thorax' means chest. It's blood inside the chest cavity. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which mental health condition is common in women experiencing flashbacks and severe anxiety linked to FGM trauma?

options.A: Schizophrenia
options.B: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
options.C: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
options.D: Bipolar disorder

explanation: Well done! PTSD happens when the mind struggles to process heavy physical and emotional trauma, leading to flashbacks and constant anxiety. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T4#GNS225_U6_T4_h5)

question: Why is it smart to check inside a patient's mouth with a penlight after they finish a meal?

options.A: To check for leftover food pockets that could lead to aspiration
options.B: To ensure the patient has brushed their own teeth properly
options.C: To check if the patient's dentures need permanent resizing
options.D: To measure the exact pH of the remaining saliva

explanation: Patients with weak mouth muscles often hoard food in their cheeks. Finding and clearing those pockets prevents food from sliding into the airway later! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h6)

question: What routine self-care practice is strongly emphasized to patients at risk for infective endocarditis to prevent bacteria from entering the bloodstream?

options.A: Refusing all routine vaccinations at local health clinics
options.B: Drinking large quantities of palm wine daily
options.C: Maintaining good oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise for the rest of their lives

explanation: Oral bacteria can easily enter the bloodstream during dental procedures or daily hygiene, making dental care a primary prevention target for endocarditis. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h8)

question: Which type of sensory receptors inside the ear pick up sound and movement?

options.A: Chemoreceptors
options.B: Photoreceptors
options.C: Thermoreceptors
options.D: Mechanoreceptors

explanation: Think 'mechanical'! Mechanoreceptors respond to physical forces like sound waves and fluid movement in the ear. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T2#GNS211_U4_T2_h1)

question: A new mother at a health post starts bleeding heavily and looks dizzy and pale. What are your first nursing steps?

options.A: Encourage the patient to stand up and walk around to stimulate circulation
options.B: Apply a warm compress to the patient's forehead and offer oral fluids
options.C: Wait quietly for two hours to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.D: Perform uterine massage, give oxytocin, and prepare for emergency referral

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is an emergency. Massaging the uterus and giving oxytocin helps it contract while you arrange urgent transfer. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h4)

question: What does a genitourinary neoplasm involve?

options.A: Inflammation of the prostate gland caused by pathogens
options.B: Chronic bacterial infections of the lower urinary tract
options.C: Abnormal tissue growths in the urinary and male reproductive systems
options.D: Sudden loss of kidney filtration due to dehydration

explanation: Think of a neoplasm simply as an abnormal growth or tumor. When we say genitourinary, we mean the organs of the urinary system and the male reproductive tract. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h1)

question: What shape does a single smooth muscle cell usually have?

options.A: Short, branched, and connected by intercalated discs
options.B: Spindle-shaped with a single central nucleus
options.C: Flat and square with rough borders
options.D: Long and cylindrical with multiple nuclei

explanation: Think of them like little tapered grains of rice—thicker in the middle and pointed at the ends, holding just one cozy nucleus right in the center. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h2)

question: Why do people often get confused by the word 'stress' in stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: They believe it is caused by mental exhaustion
options.B: They assume it only happens during high-intensity sports
options.C: They confuse it with neurological distress
options.D: They think it relates to emotional anxiety rather than physical pressure

explanation: It's an easy mix-up! In this case, 'stress' means physical force or pressure on your organs, not emotional stress or worry. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h1)

question: What does opt-out HIV testing mean during antenatal care?

options.A: The test is performed routinely unless the woman explicitly refuses it.
options.B: Only women with visible clinical symptoms are required to take the test.
options.C: The husband must give written consent before the wife can be tested.
options.D: Testing is completely optional and only done if the patient asks for it.

explanation: Opt-out screening means HIV testing is automatically included in routine prenatal lab work, and patients must actively decline if they do not want it. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h4)

question: An older adult patient with orthostatic hypotension is preparing for discharge. What instruction should the nurse include in their care plan?

options.A: Avoid wearing compression socks because they block blood flow.
options.B: Drink less fluid during the day to avoid frequent bathroom trips.
options.C: Stand up as quickly as possible to get blood moving.
options.D: Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before standing up.

explanation: Sitting on the edge of the bed allows the cardiovascular system to adjust to posture changes, preventing orthostatic dizziness. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h7)

options.C: The total absence of any identifiable bacteria in the blood
options.D: A static condition achieved strictly through pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health isn't just the literal absence of sickness. In nursing, we see it as a flowing, everyday state of overall physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the most common early sign of endometrial cancer?

options.A: Postmenopausal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Swelling in both lower legs
options.C: Severe lower back pain
options.D: Rapid unintended weight loss

explanation: You nailed it! Any bleeding or spotting after menopause is a red flag that always needs a doctor's attention. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T23#GNS216_U5_T23_h4)

question: Why do doctors perform a colposcopy and take a biopsy after a woman gets an abnormal Pap smear result?

options.A: To clean out the entire uterine cavity and prevent future infections
options.B: To examine suspicious areas closely and take a tissue sample for definitive diagnosis
options.C: To measure the exact hormone levels circulating in the pelvic blood vessels
options.D: To instantly cure the viral infection using high-intensity light beams

explanation: Think of a Pap smear as a warning bell, while a colposcopy and biopsy are the detectives that look closer to confirm what is really going on. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h5)

question: If a brain tumor starts growing inside the skull, what has to happen first to keep pressure from rising too high?

options.A: Brain neurons must shrink in size to increase internal air pockets.
options.B: The bones of the skull must stretch outward to create more space.
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid or blood volume must decrease to compensate.
options.D: Systemic heart rate must drop to zero to halt blood entering the head.

explanation: Since an adult skull cannot stretch, the body makes room for the new mass by pushing out some CSF or blood. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T19#GNS222_U3_T19_h3)

question: Why does the body use fibrinolysis after a blood vessel has finished healing?

options.A: To prevent the platelets from sticking to healthy tissue
options.B: To stimulate rapid production of new red blood cells
options.C: To trigger the initial vascular constriction phase
options.D: To remove the unnecessary clot and restore normal blood flow

explanation: Once the vessel repair is complete, the body doesn't need that old clot anymore. Fibrinolysis cleans it up so blood can flow smoothly again without blockages! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h1)

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries?

options.A: Filtering waste and storing urine
options.B: Producing red blood cells and digesting fats
options.C: Producing gametes and secreting sex hormones
options.D: Manufacturing mucus and housing fetal tissue

explanation: The ovaries create egg cells and release hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h5)

question: How do nursing assistants contribute to the healthcare team during custodial care?

options.A: They prescribe complex pharmacological drugs and diagnose medical diseases.
options.B: They perform major surgical procedures in home environments.
options.C: They observe daily changes in the client and report them to professional nurses.
options.D: They handle hospital finance bills and insurance policies.

explanation: While nursing assistants do not diagnose or treat, they spend the most time with clients and serve as vital observers who report new symptoms or changes. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the main function of the epididymis?

options.A: Neutralize acidic urine in the urethra
options.B: Allow sperm to mature and gain motility
options.C: Secrete the majority of seminal fluid
options.D: Produce primary male sex hormones

explanation: Sperm entering the epididymis are not yet able to swim; they store there while maturing and acquiring motility. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h3)

question: Your patient starts having trouble breathing and facial swelling right after a new IV antibiotic starts. What should you do first?

options.A: Stop the infusion immediately and notify the doctor.
options.B: Give the patient a glass of water and tell them to rest.
options.C: Write an incident report for the pharmacy department.
options.D: Slow down the drip rate and wait to see if it stops.

explanation: Patient safety first! Always stop the offending drug right away to prevent things from getting worse before calling the doctor. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is the main job of sodium fluoride inside the blood collection tube?

options.A: It stains white blood cells for the microscope
options.B: It speeds up blood clotting so serum separates instantly
options.C: It stops blood cells from consuming the glucose inside the tube
options.D: It stops the blood sample from freezing during transport

explanation: Think of sodium fluoride as a preservative. Without it, the living blood cells inside the tube would keep eating up the glucose, giving you a falsely low lab result! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h4)

question: Which organs are prioritized and receive redirected blood flow during early shock?

options.A: The kidneys and the stomach
options.B: The skin and the skeletal muscles
options.C: The liver and the intestines
options.D: The brain and the heart

explanation: The body's survival reflex constricts vessels in less vital areas like the skin and gut to ensure the brain and heart continue to receive oxygen. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h2)

question: A nurse wipes down a bedside table with a chemical disinfectant. What is the expected result?

options.A: Most pathogenic germs are killed, but bacterial spores may survive
options.B: The surface becomes completely sterile for surgical procedures
options.C: All living microorganisms and tough spores are completely destroyed
options.D: Only visible dust and physical dirt are physically washed away

explanation: Disinfectants are great for cleaning surfaces and killing most harmful germs, but they don't always wipe out tough bacterial spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient with severe nephrotic syndrome is most likely to report which initial pattern of swelling?

options.A: Severe swelling limited to the toes
options.B: Sudden swelling of only the right hand
options.C: Puffiness around the eyes upon waking up
options.D: Throbbing pain and swelling in the jaw

explanation: Periorbital edema is a classic early sign of fluid shifting into loose facial tissues overnight while the patient is lying flat. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h3)

question: A patient with right-sided weakness is walking with a cane for the first time. Where should you stand?

options.A: A few steps ahead to pull the patient forward
options.B: Directly in front of the patient facing backwards
options.C: On the patient's stronger left side
options.D: On the patient's weaker right side

explanation: Always stay close to the side that needs the most support so you can steady them right away if they lean or slip. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T4#GNS221_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient is admitted with severe vomiting and diarrhea. Which imbalance are they most at risk for developing?

options.A: Fluid and electrolyte imbalance
options.B: Excessive weight gain
options.C: Permanent high blood pressure
options.D: Chronic respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Exactly! Vomiting and diarrhea flush out body fluids and essential minerals super fast, leaving the patient low on water and electrolytes. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which part of the brain acts like the main switchboard to keep us awake?

options.A: Basal ganglia
options.B: Occipital cortex
options.C: Reticular activating system
options.D: Cerebellar vermis

explanation: Think of the reticular activating system in the brainstem as the master 'wake-up' switch for the whole brain. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why are transcutaneous (skin) bilirubin readings often followed up with a blood test when numbers are high?

options.A: Skin devices can be influenced by skin tone and are only meant for screening
options.B: Transcutaneous meters measure direct bilirubin instead of total bilirubin
options.C: Skin readings only work accurately after the baby is two weeks old
options.D: Blood tests are required by law before a baby can start breastfeeding

explanation: Handheld skin scanners are wonderful for quick checks, but a blood test gives us the exact numbers needed for treatment decisions. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h6)

question: How many layers make up the standard triple packaging system for infectious substances?

options.A: Three layers
options.B: One layer
options.C: Two layers
options.D: Four layers

explanation: The system consists of a primary receptacle, secondary packaging, and an outer packaging layer working together. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h4)

question: You are caring for a stroke patient who has trouble swallowing (dysphagia). What must you check first before giving them anything to eat or drink?

options.A: Perform a proper swallow screen and ensure the patient sits upright
options.B: Administer a strong sleeping pill to calm the patient down
options.C: Give the patient a large glass of cold water to test throat reflexes
options.D: Place the patient completely flat on their back in bed

explanation: Swallowing issues put patients at high risk of choking or getting food in their lungs (aspiration). Always check their swallow reflex and keep them sitting upright! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h4)

question: A school nurse notices several students rubbing their eyes and squinting at the chalkboard. What should she do?

options.A: Vision screening assessments
options.B: Playground safety audits
options.C: Emergency vaccination drives
options.D: Nutritional cooking classes

explanation: You nailed it! Squinting at the board is a classic sign of eye trouble, so a quick vision check is the best next step. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of genetic counseling for families affected by these disorders?

options.A: To provide daily physical therapy for weakened muscles
options.B: To prescribe medication for muscle spasms and pain
options.C: To perform surgical procedures that repair damaged genes
options.D: To explain inheritance risks and guide family planning decisions

explanation: Genetic counselors help families understand how a condition is passed down and discuss testing options for other relatives. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h7)

question: Some food handlers are struggling with hygiene rules because they find English difficult. What should the nurse supervisor do?

options.A: Stop doing hygiene training and rely only on surprise inspections
options.B: Punish the workers for failing to read the English instruction manual
options.C: Conduct training sessions using the local language and visual demonstrations
options.D: Report the workers to the police for breaking environmental laws

explanation: Adapting how you teach to match your audience ensures everyone understands these life-saving safety practices. Great clinical judgment! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h7)

question: How should you as a nurse view a dying patient's refusal to eat and drink?

options.A: As an urgent sign to start artificial tube feeding right away
options.B: As a normal part of the body shutting down its digestive functions
options.C: As a psychological sign of severe hopelessness
options.D: As a sign that the patient has a blocked bowel

explanation: The digestive system naturally slows down at the end of life. Forcing food or water can actually cause nausea and discomfort. Trust your training! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of triage during a mass casualty disaster?

options.A: To collect insurance and payment details from victims
options.B: To sort and prioritize patients based on injury severity
options.C: To discharge healthy staff members so they can go home
options.D: To clean and disinfect the emergency room floors

explanation: Triage allows medical personnel to quickly identify and treat those with life-threatening injuries first when resources are limited. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why are standard Alzheimer's drugs usually avoided or used carefully in Pick's disease?

options.A: They accelerate memory loss within the first week of use.
options.B: They interfere with routine blood pressure medications.
options.C: They do not target the underlying pathology and can worsen agitation.
options.D: They cause immediate and permanent paralysis of the lower limbs.

explanation: Alzheimer's medications don't help frontotemporal issues and can actually make behavioral outbursts worse. It's a great clinical pearl to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h5)

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient right after placing a sublingual tablet?

options.A: Drink a full glass of water immediately to wash it down.
options.B: Lie flat on your back for at least one hour.
options.C: Do not eat, drink, or smoke until the pill is fully dissolved.
options.D: Chew the tablet quickly to help it enter the bloodstream.

explanation: Eating or drinking washes the medication away before it can absorb through the oral mucosa. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of severe, untreated skin disorders?

options.A: Permanent structural damage to internal kidney tissue from skin flakes
options.B: Impairment of the skin's ability to regulate body temperature
options.C: Secondary bacterial skin infections like cellulitis or impetigo
options.D: Profound psychosocial distress and social anxiety

explanation: Spot on! Skin issues can cause local infections, temperature trouble, and emotional stress, but flaky skin alone won't damage your kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h8)

question: What does 'monitoring' primarily involve in community health programs?

options.A: Continuous tracking of service uptake and activities
options.B: Waiting until a five-year grant period finishes
options.C: Changing the geographic location of the clinic daily
options.D: Firing staff members who fail to meet quotas

explanation: Monitoring is an ongoing process of tracking day-to-day activities and service delivery metrics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h7)

question: Why does cigarette smoking increase a woman's chance of getting cervical cancer?

options.A: Tobacco smoke alters systemic blood pressure in the pelvic organs
options.B: Byproducts in tobacco smoke weaken local immunity and damage cervical cells
options.C: Smoking causes immediate permanent closure of the internal cervical os
options.D: Nicotine directly destroys all protective antibodies inside the uterus

explanation: Think of cigarette smoke as carrying harmful chemicals that settle in cervical mucus, wearing down local defenses and damaging cell DNA. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h3)

question: Which lab finding under a microscope points strongly to a kidney infection (pyelonephritis) rather than a simple bladder infection?

options.A: Calcium oxalate crystals
options.B: Squamous epithelial cells
options.C: White blood cell casts
options.D: Isolated red blood cells

explanation: Casts are tiny mold-shaped clumps that form way up inside the kidney tubes. Finding white cell casts tells us the infection has traveled high up into the kidneys! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h4)

question: How is Family Life Education different from clinical therapy?

options.A: Education requires a medical doctor license whereas therapy does not
options.B: Education is only practiced inside hospitals while therapy is done in schools
options.C: Education focuses on prevention and growth while therapy often focuses on remediation
options.D: Education deals exclusively with infants while therapy is for the elderly

explanation: You got it! Think of education as building strong life skills early, while therapy steps in later to help heal and fix existing emotional or relationship struggles. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h1)

question: Which specific bone cells are responsible for breaking down or resorbing bone tissue?

options.A: Osteons
options.B: Osteoblasts
options.C: Osteocytes
options.D: Osteoclasts

explanation: Remember: Osteoclasts 'c'rve or 'c'ut bone down! They break down old bone tissue to help with remodeling and keep blood calcium levels balanced. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T1#GNS222_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the ultimate goal of home health nursing?

options.A: Replacing all family involvement in patient care
options.B: Helping the patient achieve maximum independence
options.C: Transferring the patient to a permanent nursing home
options.D: Keeping the patient dependent on daily nursing visits

explanation: Home health nursing focuses heavily on empowering patients to manage their own care and daily routines safely. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T5#GNS324_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which symptom is a very common clue that points specifically to COVID-19 over other flu-like viruses?

options.A: Sudden loss of taste or smell
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.D: Severe swelling of the salivary glands

explanation: Spot on! Losing your sense of taste or smell (anosmia and ageusia) is a classic hallmark sign of a SARS-CoV-2 infection. Easy to remember for your clinicals! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of print IEC material?

options.A: Illustrated leaflets and posters
options.B: Radio jingles and community songs
options.C: Traditional dance and town criers
options.D: Live theatrical drama skits

explanation: Print materials rely on visual text and graphics, such as leaflets, flyers, and posters, to convey health messages. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is evaluated when assessing the sensory system during a neurological exam?

options.A: Light touch and pain perception
options.B: Muscle bulk and involuntary twitching
options.C: Deep tendon reflex hammer response
options.D: Level of orientation to time and place

explanation: Sensory evaluations focus on how well the patient perceives external stimuli like touch, pain, and vibration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h4)

question: How does understanding a client's cultural background improve psychosocial nursing care?

options.A: It reduces the cost of hospital medications.
options.B: It allows the nurse to change the client's religious practices.
options.C: It proves which medical treatment is the only correct option.
options.D: It helps the nurse respect the client's beliefs about illness and healing.

explanation: Cultural awareness builds trust and ensures care plans align with the client's personal values and traditions. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which layer of the gut wall is directly responsible for pushing food forward with wave-like squeezes?

options.A: Muscularis externa
options.B: Mucosa
options.C: Submucosa
options.D: Serosa

explanation: Great job! The muscularis externa has smooth muscle layers that team up to move food smoothly along the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is a budget considered such an important financial tool?

options.A: It provides a clear benchmark to compare actual spending against planned goals
options.B: It automatically generates profits without requiring staff work
options.C: It gives nurse managers unlimited power to hire any staff they want
options.D: It stops patients from ever questioning their hospital bills

explanation: A budget sets a clear target so managers can check whether the unit is staying on track or spending too much. [learn more](GST321_U1_T23#GST321_U1_T23_h4)

question: Which mental health challenge is commonly seen in teenage mothers after childbirth?

options.A: Postpartum depression
options.B: Schizophrenic psychosis
options.C: Bipolar manic disorder
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive hoarding

explanation: The sudden shift to parenting, lack of emotional maturity, and feeling alone place teenage mothers at high risk for postpartum depression. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is a great example of a short-term rehabilitation goal?

options.A: Moving back into a completely independent apartment
options.B: Driving a personal vehicle across the country
options.C: Securing a full-time job in the community
options.D: Learning to transfer safely from bed to wheelchair

explanation: Small steps lead to big victories! Moving safely from bed to chair is a vital foundational skill needed early on. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T1#GNS123_U6_T1_h3)

question: What should a patient do right after taking a puff from a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: Hold their breath for about 10 seconds
options.B: Exhale rapidly through the nose three times
options.C: Lie flat on the bed to rest the chest muscles
options.D: Take a sip of water right away without spitting

explanation: Holding the breath gives the medicine time to settle deep into the airways instead of just floating right back out when the patient exhales. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h3)

question: Which of these statements about injectable contraceptives is FALSE?

options.A: They prevent pregnancy by stopping ovulation
options.B: They require regular repeat doses to remain effective
options.C: They lead to permanent sterility after one dose
options.D: They can cause changes in monthly bleeding patterns

explanation: Injectables do not cause permanent infertility! Once you stop, fertility naturally returns after the drug clears the system. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h5)

question: Why is it important to check the electrical cord of the steam generator before turning it on?

options.A: To verify the correct voltage for the hospital room
options.B: To measure how much electricity the unit will use
options.C: To ensure the heating water boils much faster
options.D: To prevent electrical shocks and fire hazards

explanation: Spot on! Water and electricity are a dangerous mix, so checking cords keeps both you and your patient safe. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which hormones flood the body right away during a sudden 'fight-or-flight' moment?

options.A: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.B: Epinephrine and norepinephrine
options.C: Estrogen and progesterone
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: When you get a sudden fright, your adrenal medulla instantly pumps out adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline to get your body ready to run or fight! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT required under standard precautions for a routine physical check?

options.A: Wearing clean gloves if contact with body fluids is expected
options.B: Cleaning stethoscope bells and diaphragms between patients
options.C: Performing proper hand hygiene before touching the patient
options.D: Wearing a full sterile surgical gown for a simple pulse check

explanation: Routine physical checks do not require sterile surgical gowns unless you are performing a sterile invasive procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: In the ACHES warning acronym for oral contraceptives, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Chest pain
options.B: Cramping
options.C: Constipation
options.D: Coughing

explanation: The ACHES mnemonic is a nursing classic! 'C' stands for chest pain, which can point to serious issues like a blood clot in the lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h7)

question: What is the primary role of red bone marrow found inside bones?

options.A: Storing excess body fat
options.B: Producing new blood cells
options.C: Releasing calcium into joints
options.D: Filtering waste from blood

explanation: Red bone marrow contains stem cells responsible for creating red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T1#GNS222_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must a stroke client pass a swallow test before you give them normal food?

options.A: To check if the client has an allergy to hospital cutlery
options.B: To prevent food from entering the airway and causing aspiration pneumonia
options.C: To ensure the stomach can digest heavy proteins and fats
options.D: To find out which specific food flavors the client prefers to eat

explanation: Stroke weakness can make throat muscles sluggish, meaning food or water can easily slip down the 'wrong pipe' into the lungs instead of the belly. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h7)

question: Which of these is considered a physical workplace hazard?

options.A: Hepatitis B virus exposure
options.B: Toxic chemical solvents
options.C: Excessive industrial noise
options.D: Heavy psychological stress

explanation: You nailed it! Physical hazards include things like loud noise, extreme temperatures, and vibrations that can wear down your health over time. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h4)

question: Why do nurses always tell patients to take levothyroxine on an empty stomach?

options.A: Food neutralizes the stomach acid needed to activate the tablet
options.B: Food and certain minerals in the gut can reduce the drug's absorption
options.C: The drug causes severe stomach ulcers if mixed with food proteins
options.D: Taking it with food causes immediate destruction of the liver

explanation: Things like calcium, iron, and heavy meals can trap the drug in your gut and stop it from getting into your bloodstream where it's needed. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T2#GNS223_U7_T2_h3)

question: Why do we strictly control the movement of people inside a surgical suite?

options.A: To ensure the nurses finish their paperwork on time
options.B: To make sure doctors do not get lost in the hospital
options.C: To keep the surgical equipment from being stolen
options.D: To prevent the spread of microorganisms into sterile areas

explanation: Exactly! Limiting unnecessary movement means less dust and fewer germs floating around, which helps keep the surgical field super clean and safe. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h1)

question: A patient is getting a CT scan with contrast dye for an adrenal tumor. What is a vital nursing check beforehand?

options.A: Measuring the patient's 24-hour urine cortisol
options.B: Checking for allergies to iodine or shellfish
options.C: Testing the patient for active thyroid antibodies
options.D: Ensuring the patient has swallowed radioactive iodine

explanation: Safety first! Contrast dye often contains iodine, so checking for allergies beforehand helps prevent severe allergic reactions. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is feeling the uterus during a physical assessment so important when suspecting postpartum endometritis?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the organ
options.B: To check for tenderness and a boggy texture
options.C: To test the strength of the pelvic floor muscles
options.D: To evaluate the size of the ovaries

explanation: A healthy postpartum uterus should feel firm as it shrinks back down. An infected one feels tender and soft, or 'boggy,' because it's struggling to contract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h5)

question: What extra job does propylthiouracil (PTU) do that methimazole doesn't?

options.A: Stimulating the pituitary gland to stop releasing TSH
options.B: Binding directly to circulating T3 molecules in the blood
options.C: Destroying existing thyroid tissue through direct radiation
options.D: Inhibiting the peripheral conversion of T4 into T3

explanation: Besides stopping new hormone production, PTU also slows down how T4 turns into the active T3 hormone in the body's tissues. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T3#GNS223_U7_T3_h2)

question: If an older male patient has an enlarged prostate (BPH), what urinary symptom is he most likely to complain about?

options.A: A weak and slow urinary stream
options.B: Total absence of urine production
options.C: Inability to control bowel movements
options.D: Severe pain during bladder filling

explanation: Makes total sense, right? When the prostate grows, it presses on the urethra like a pinched garden hose, making the urine flow slow and weak. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary benefit of establishing a coordinated referral pathway for GBV survivors?

options.A: It prevents the survivor from having to repeat their traumatic story to every new agency
options.B: It guarantees that the perpetrator will receive a life prison sentence
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to document physical injuries
options.D: It automatically lowers the hospital's electricity and water bills

explanation: Seamless coordination reduces secondary trauma by sparing survivors from retelling painful details at every step. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h7)

question: Why can early diagnosis of genitourinary cancers sometimes be delayed?

options.A: Blood tests usually show completely normal results for years
options.B: Patients refuse to provide urine samples during routine visits
options.C: Tumors in these organs never cause any noticeable signs
options.D: Their early symptoms often mimic common urinary tract infections

explanation: Symptoms like burning when you pee or seeing a little blood can easily be mistaken for a simple UTI, which is why sometimes treatment gets delayed while trying antibiotics first. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h5)

question: A newborn has a heart rate of 110, pink body with blue hands, a strong cry, and pulls away when touched. What score do they get for muscle tone (Activity)?

options.A: Score of 1 for some flexion
options.B: Score of 2 for weak cry
options.C: Score of 0 for limp tone
options.D: Score of 2 for active motion

explanation: Active movement and good flexion of the arms and legs show great muscle tone, earning the full 2 points in the Apgar activity check. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h1)

question: Why is ophthalmoscopy useful for monitoring chronic systemic diseases like diabetes?

options.A: It directly measures the current level of sugar floating in the blood
options.B: It reveals early vascular damage in the tiny retinal blood vessels
options.C: It tracks how well the kidneys are filtering waste from the body
options.D: It calculates the total amount of protein stored in body tissues

question: What causes that unpleasant smell in some gas?

options.A: Sulfur compounds produced by specific gut bacteria
options.B: The breakdown of proteins by liver enzymes
options.C: High levels of pure oxygen from swallowed air
options.D: Undigested stomach acid reaching the rectum

explanation: Certain helpful (and smelly!) bacteria release tiny amounts of sulfur when they break down food. Totally normal body process! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why do we run lab tests and checks for patients in the intensive care unit (ICU)?

options.A: To replace the standard physical assessment entirely
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of hospital stays
options.C: To track how well current treatments are working
options.D: To shorten the nursing shift handover time

explanation: Think of lab tests and diagnostics as your patient's report card. They give us real-time clues to see if our care is helping or if things are taking a turn. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h1)

question: A patient is having a hard time buttoning their shirt and holding a toothbrush after a stroke. Who should step in to help with these daily tasks?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists are experts at helping patients regain fine motor skills for daily activities like dressing, eating, and brushing teeth. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h2)

question: Six hours after delivery, a mom feels dizzy. You check and find her uterus is soft (boggy) and pushed to the right. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Prepare the patient for immediate major surgery
options.B: Massage the uterine fundus until firm and encourage bladder emptying
options.C: Administer oral pain relievers and tell her to sleep
options.D: Check her blood glucose level and offer juice

explanation: A boggy uterus means it's relaxing and bleeding could start! Massaging it helps it contract, and getting her to empty her bladder will stop it from being pushed out of place. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h7)

question: Where does Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) fit into the safety hierarchy for handling workplace hazards?

options.A: It is the last line of defense after other controls
options.B: It is only required after a toxic exposure has occurred
options.C: It replaces the need for proper chemical labelling
options.D: It is the primary method to eliminate workplace hazards

explanation: That's correct! PPE depends entirely on human behavior and proper wear, making it our last safety net if other controls fail. We always prefer removing the danger first. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h5)

question: Why must the packaging used for steam sterilization be porous (able to let air and steam through)?

options.A: To ensure the wrapper dissolves completely inside the machine
options.B: To make the heavy trays lighter for nurses to carry
options.C: To let air escape so the package smells fresh when opened
options.D: To allow the sterilizing agent to penetrate and reach the instruments

explanation: Brilliant! Steam needs to touch every single surface of the tools inside to actually kill the germs. Porous wraps let the steam in safely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: What action should a nurse take when a sharps container reaches its designated fill line?

options.A: Leave it open on the counter until the end of the working week
options.B: Seal and close the container securely for safe disposal
options.C: Push the needles down firmly with a gloved hand to create more space
options.D: Transfer some of the used needles into a regular plastic trash bag

explanation: Containers must be closed and replaced once they reach the fill line to prevent accidental overflows and needle injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the term for the uterus shrinking back down to its normal size after birth?

options.A: Fundal subinvolution
options.B: Uterine involution
options.C: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.D: Myometrial contraction

explanation: Think of 'involution' as the uterus gracefully rolling back down to its pre-pregnancy size. Great midwifery term to know! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h2)

question: Why is cultural awareness especially important for rehabilitation nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: It speeds up the pharmacological action of prescribed drugs
options.B: It replaces the need for standard clinical assessments
options.C: It is required by international hospital accreditation bodies
options.D: It helps nurses adapt care plans to fit the patient's home environment and beliefs

explanation: Understanding local traditions and family structures ensures that rehabilitation goals are realistic and culturally acceptable to the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h1)

question: How should you write down a patient's main complaint in their case notes?

options.A: As a summarized medical diagnosis written by the nurse
options.B: By translating slang into professional clinical terminology
options.C: In the patient's own words using quotation marks
options.D: Using a standardized 1 to 10 numeric severity scale

explanation: You nailed it! Using their exact words in quotes keeps their true perspective alive in the record. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main goal of diagnostic testing for hormone (endocrine) disorders?

options.A: To destroy overactive hormone-producing tissue
options.B: To permanently replace missing organ functions
options.C: To cure infectious agents causing gland failure
options.D: To measure hormone levels and check organ response

explanation: You've got this! Endocrine tests simply check how much hormone is in the body and see how target organs respond to signals. It is all about checking the balance. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is your main nursing goal when caring for a patient who just suffered an animal bite or insect sting?

options.A: Discharge the patient with mild analgesics
options.B: Administer broad-spectrum oral antibiotics immediately
options.C: Perform surgical debridement of the wound
options.D: Halt toxin exposure and stabilize vital signs

explanation: Great job thinking emergency care! Before cleaning any wound, your priority is making sure the venom stops spreading and the patient's breathing and pulse are steady. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h1)
